concepts.def: Cell with a nucleus (e.g. animal, plant, fungi)
Organelle holding DNA in a eukaryotic cell
Protein that speeds up reactions in living things

walkthroughs.body_html:
All cells have a membrane, cytoplasm and DNA.

Eukaryotes have nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes. Plants add cell wall, chloroplasts, permanent vacuole. Prokaryotes have plasmids and a DNA loop.

Light microscopes magnify up to ×2000, resolution ~200 nm. Electron microscopes magnify up to ×1 000 000, resolution ~0.2 nm.

Electron microscopes show organelles — but the sample must be dead and prepared.

Substrate fits the active site like a key in a lock. The enzyme speeds up the reaction without being used up.

High temperatures or wrong pH denature the enzyme — active site changes shape.

mcqs.q: Which organelle holds the DNA in a eukaryote?
options: Nucleus
Mitochondrion
Ribosome
Vacuole

mcqs.q: Which structure do plant cells have that animal cells do NOT?
options: Cell wall
Cell membrane
Nucleus
Cytoplasm

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Enzymes choose their substrate based on which one is most common in the cell.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.

mcqs.q: What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: The enzyme has been completely broken into amino acids.
Enzymes choose their substrate based on which one is most common in the cell.
Its tertiary structure (3D shape) changes, particularly the active site, so it can no longer bind substrate effectively.
The enzyme has died because enzymes are alive.

mcqs.q: Why are enzymes specific to certain substrates?
options: Only substrates with complementary shape and chemistry to the active site can bind effectively.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Enzymes choose their substrate based on which one is most common in the cell.
Each enzyme can react with any substrate, but works fastest with one type.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryote”?
options: Cell with a nucleus (e.g. animal, plant, fungi)
Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate
Protein that speeds up reactions in living things
Organelle holding DNA in a eukaryotic cell

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Specificity”?

Cell without a nucleus (e.g. bacteria)
Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate
Each enzyme only fits one type of substrate

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Active site”?
options: Each enzyme only fits one type of substrate
Cell without a nucleus (e.g. bacteria)
Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate
Cell with a nucleus (e.g. animal, plant, fungi)

Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate

options: Cell without a nucleus (e.g. bacteria)
Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate
Protein that speeds up reactions in living things
Organelle holding DNA in a eukaryotic cell

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Enzyme”?
options: Cell with a nucleus (e.g. animal, plant, fungi)
Region of an enzyme that binds its substrate

mcqs.q: Maximum useful magnification of a school light microscope:
A student calculates magnification as image size ÷ actual size. An image is 30 mm and the actual object is 0.06 mm. What is the magnification?
An enzyme is described as specific. The best explanation is that:
options: Its active site fits only a complementary substrate.
It can speed up any reaction in the cell.
It is used up after each reaction.
It works only at very high temperatures.

mcqs.q: Which feature is present in a eukaryotic cell but absent in a prokaryotic cell?
options: A membrane-bound nucleus
A cell membrane
Cytoplasm
Ribosomes

mcqs.q: A reaction catalysed by an enzyme slows almost to a stop after the solution is boiled. The best explanation is that:
options: The enzyme has denatured and its active site changed shape.
The substrate evaporated when heated.
The enzyme was used up by the reaction.
Boiling added more substrate.
